title: Add validated global upload and download bandwidth limits
description:
Fork research: parallel GPT-6 Astra source reviews, 2026-10-25. Current application baseline: 3ae404b.

## Purpose and evidence

Simple Torrent and covrom expose bandwidth controls; current Config has only upload/seeding booleans. Independent global limits would prevent transfers saturating a shared link. Reimplement the behavior rather than copying either fork: boypt treats invalid input as unlimited, and covrom wires a one-token-per-second limiter with misleading burst units.

## Acceptance criteria

- Expose independent global upload/download caps with explicit consistent units and an explicit unlimited value. Persist settings and regenerate types for the existing settings UI.
- Reject negative, nonfinite, malformed or overflowing values atomically and preserve the current valid setting. Invalid input must never silently become unlimited.
- Apply sustained aggregate limits with documented burst tolerance, including relevant peer and webseed payload paths. Avoid client replacement when safe limiter updates are available; preserve stopped/running state and selections.
- Validate actual throttled throughput in both directions with deterministic local peers/webseeds, plus unlimited mode, runtime updates and invalid-value rejection. Do not assert only limiter configuration fields.

## Sources

- https://github.com/boypt/simple-torrent/blob/6f4942933b71106bae00b4f4c94438e3b315fca2/engine/engine.go#L103-L107
- https://github.com/boypt/simple-torrent/blob/6f4942933b71106bae00b4f4c94438e3b315fca2/engine/utils.go#L18-L47
- https://github.com/boypt/simple-torrent/blob/6f4942933b71106bae00b4f4c94438e3b315fca2/engine/config.go#L155-L171
- https://github.com/covrom/cloud-torrent/blob/96fe65ee3121752f31da5e7170b2c18ffda272d7/engine/engine.go#L60-L65
- https://github.com/jpillora/cloud-torrent/blob/3ae404b282d7678f90e16b0bf84a52d872fc73d9/engine/config.go

## Scope

Implement within the existing Go engine, typed API, generated frontend models and authenticated handler chain. Use isolated legal fixtures; never test against live downloads. This is a new backlog item, not a claim that the proposed behavior already exists.
